data.title: mTOR complex 2 is required for the development of prostate cancer induced by Pten loss in mice
data.authors: Guertin DA; Sabatini DM et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mTORC2 is required for prostate cancer driven by Pten loss in mice.
data.abstract_excerpt: mTOR complex 2 (mTORC2) contains the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) kinase and the Rictor regulatory protein and phosphorylates Akt. Whether this function of mTORC2 is critical for cancer progression is unknown. Here, we show that transformed human prostate epithelial cells lacking PTEN require mTORC2 to form tumors when injected into nude mice. Furthermore, we find that Rictor is a haploinsufficient gene and that deleting one copy protects Pten heterozygous mice from prostate cancer.

extracted_findings.effect: mTORC2 is required for prostate cancer driven by Pten loss; Rictor is haploinsufficient
extracted_findings.sample_size: Pten +/- mice (n=9), Pten +/- Rictor +/- mice (n=10), wild-type controls (n=10) for prostate cancer analysis.
extracted_findings.effect_size: PC-3 xenografts: shLuc-expressing cells formed tumors of 312 mm 3; shRictor 1 and shRictor 2 cells formed tumors of 10.1 mm 3 (p=0.01) and 39.6 mm 3 (p=0.01). Ki67 positive cells: 2.3% in Pten +/- Rictor +/- vs 10.7% in Pten +/- (p < 0.001).
extracted_findings.limitations: Specific inhibitors of mTORC2 are unavailable, precluding pharmacological testing. Differences in genetic background between Rictor +/- mice and mtor/Raptor/mlst8 heterozygous mice precluded prostate cancer analysis in some cohorts.
